newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-IRSG sees modest growth in '98 rubber demand.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-IRSG sees modest growth in '98 rubber demand.

text.p: World rubber consumption is expected to grow a modest 3.0 percent in 1998 after a 3.6 percent expansion in 1997 with the synthetic rubber's share of the global use taking a further dip.

International Rubber Study Group (IRSG), releasing its latest statistics after its 101st meeting, said Friday the share of synthetic rubber could fall to 60.9 percent in 1998 from 61.0 percent in 1997 and 70.5 percent in 1979.
But the slide is slowing down and the share of the consumption is expected to stabilise at a level slightly lower than the current estimate of 60.4 percent during 1997-2000.
IRSG secretary-general Maurice Cain told reporters that the rubber industry was headed into a period of continued growth in demand.

"The major consumer of rubber, the tyre industry, continues to expand its production and its geographical spread. The predicted saturation in the tyre markets in the United States and Europe is more than offset by the rapidly increasing demand in the southeast Asia," he said.
But he said the prospects for future supply were less assured. Unless demand is lower than forecast a shortage seems inevitable, he said.
The IRSG groups 21 major rubber producing and consuming countries. It provides a forum for members to discuss matters affecting the supply and demand for both natural and synthetic rubber.
The group's data show that world natural rubber consumption will rise to 6.61 million tonnes in 1998 from 6.40 million in 1997 and 6.15 million in 1996.
Production will increase to 6.72 million in 1998 from 6.49 million in 1997 and 6.25 million in 1996.
But synthetic rubber demand and supply is expected to balance at about 10.30 million tonnes in 1998 and 10.0 million in 1997, the IRSG said.
